#### What is it? - [ ] Bugfix (user facing) - [x] Feature (user facing) - [x] Codebase improvement (dev facing) - [ ] Meta improvement to the project (dev facing) #### Description of the changes in your PR This PR massively improves the handling of player errors. It consist of 2 parts: #### 1. Improving the player error handling Up to this PR player errors are always just reported as ![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40789489/134232359-8848b4f0-b488-424d-beeb-1b2ab4feeb04.png) (or similar) This PR introduces an option (default=off) to report the Error directly (via acra): https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40789489/134233077-f92c9680-4800-47f3-a23a-65f3748c40f6.mp4 #### 2. Added an option to simulate player errors To simulate errors a debug option was introduced to crash the player. Notes: * This option is only available when using a Debug version of the app (the same as the ``DebugSettingsFragment``) * To make this work in all player variants (main, mini, background, popup) it was added to``VideoDetailFragment`` - otherwise at least sometimes there is no UI where the error can be triggered from. * This is not a true Exoplayer error as it's not possible to crash the player internally (we would have to mess up the streaming data or something similar) therefore ``Player#onPlayerError`` is simply called with an exception * When no player is available (because e.g. it was crashed) a toast shows up
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40789489/134235788-a2de5f38-1807-4d35-9ab1-da4df6856804.png) #### Fixes the following issue(s) - Fixes #7008 #### APK testing The APK can be found by going to the "Checks" tab below the title. On the left pane, click on "CI", scroll down to "artifacts" and click "app" to download the zip file which contains the debug APK of this PR. #### Due diligence - [x] I read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

I was thinking about a different approach for exceptions to report in services. I would create a new static method in the `ErrorActivity` that creates a notification (iirc two methods already exist for the two other ways to report an error, i.e. by opening the activity directly and by showing the bottom bar). Then when the user taps on the notification the error activity is opened via a `PendingIntent`.
That method could then be used in more places, e.g. in the downloader service
Having an option to change error reporting mode and showing it to the user seems complicated for them, and also introduces a new setting the user has to know about

Again, please don't introduce new settings. I'd just have this enabled in debug builds (or you can move the setting to debug) and disabled in normal builds for now. This is not a video-audio setting, this is a developer setting, the normal user should not have anything to do with it.

reply.body:
> Again, please don't introduce new settings. I'd just have this enabled in debug builds (or you can move the setting to debug) and disabled in normal builds for now. This is not a video-audio setting, this is a developer setting, the normal user should not have anything to do with it.

Why is introducing new settings a problem?
Yes this is e.g. for debugging purposes, but I don't understand why we should hide it from the user.
We may agree upon that I move the setting to the debug section. However then the debug section should also be available in the release app.

> I'd just have this disabled in normal builds since having an error popup may be disturbing.

It is disabled by default.

Btw the settings need a major overhaul: #3192

> Why is introducing new settings a problem?

If each PR added a new setting to toggle the behavior it is introducing we would have thousands of settings, of which 95% are mostly unused and the other useful 5% is difficult to find and is unknown by most users, who would not go through all thousand settings just to find out what's of interest to them. So if customizing the app becomes too difficult (and also risky I'd say, because there would be many more untested combinations), less and less people are going to really dive into it, defeating the purpose of customizability. Ad I said, the normal user does not want to see a debug setting in the video-audio settings (which is already cluttered), since it makes it difficult to find all of the others. That's why I am opposed to adding new settings unless they would be really useful for the normal user.

Therefore, for now I'd not add a new setting in normal builds and just leave the option disabled. After this PR is merged I will do an overhaul of the error handling for services, so that errors are first posted as notifications and if the user taps on them he gets to the error activity. But if the user just wants to ignore error notifications (like he can ignore the error snackbar) he can just swipe it away or even disable that notification channel in the system settings directly.

timeline.body: Instead of splitting this in three, can't the `textResId` be calculated inside the function `showPlayerError` itself? Then the function could just be called with the parameters `error, currentMetadata.getMetadata()` at the top of `onPlayerError()`.

reply.body: It's possible however then there has to be a second switch case inside  ``showPlayerError`` which has to be kept in sync with this one.
Mmmh, I don't know, I'd prefer two different switches since they do two conceptually different things, but it is also ok as it is

timeline.body: Why create a new package just for one file?

reply.body:
Structuring.

Why shouldn't I create a new package for this?
Mmmh, ok, I think of packages as a way to group similar things together, but if there is only one thing it does not make much sense to me. But let's keep it, ok.

timeline.body: I'd put `EnsureExceptionSerializable.ensureSerializable()` directly in `ErrorInfo`, so that it improves error reporting in all cases and not just for player errors.

reply.body:
``ensureSerializable`` is relatively cost insensitive and only some exceptions cause these problems. That's why I didn't put this into the default ``ErrorInfo``.
Should I still move it into there?
In my opinion yes. And, speaking of the cost, I don't think that writing ~1000 characters to a buffer, to check if the object is serializable, creates any real performance issue

timeline.body: Why use suppliers instead of simply making this class non-constructible, make all functions static and passing context and layout inflater where needed? In particular the `VideoDetailFragment` would pass `context` and `layoutInflater` in`onCrashThePlayer`.
What about making this a static field in the class instead of generating it each time?

> Or do you want to do a followup?

Yes, I'll do a followup
